question: Evaluate $$\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{11\pi}{6}\right)+\cot^{-1}\left(\cot\frac{7\pi}{4}\right).$$
explanation:
Principal value of the inverse tangent term
The principal range of $\tan^{-1}x$ is $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Since $$\tan\frac{11\pi}{6}=\tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right),$$ we obtain $$\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{11\pi}{6}\right)=-\frac{\pi}{6}.$$

Principal value of the inverse cotangent term
The principal range of $\cot^{-1}x$ is $(0,\pi)$. Also, $$\cot\frac{7\pi}{4}=-1.$$ The angle in $(0,\pi)$ whose cotangent is $-1$ is $\frac{3\pi}{4}$. Thus, $$\cot^{-1}\left(\cot\frac{7\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{3\pi}{4}.$$

Addition of principal values
Therefore, the required value is $$-\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{3\pi}{4}=\frac{-2\pi+9\pi}{12}=\frac{7\pi}{12}.$$
